## Goal
Make the operator's agent activity genuinely legible to Konrad: a Live panel that is fast and truthful, and a chat surface that shows the operator's communication with its agents. Konrad's words this morning: hovering the sidebar still lags; he cannot tell 'whether these are sub-agents of Claude Fable 5 or actually whole Claude Code sessions'; elapsed times 'are still growing even though they are done'; and in the operator chat he wants to 'see the conversations you have with them... something similar to the bash command, where I can see that you sent them a message and that you received a message from them.'

## Context
Repos in this worktree: forge-control (Hono :7700) and forge-control-web (Next 15 + React 19, pm2 forge-control-web). Live panel: app/desktop/live/AgentActivity.tsx, ManagersSection.tsx, agentsApi.ts; feed comes from /api/agents (forge-control/src/routes/agents.ts) and /api/projects/managers. Chat thread rendering: the desktop chat surface under app/desktop/ — find how Bash tool calls are rendered as collapsible blocks and mirror that pattern. Run rows live in the `runs` table (metadata.role, metadata.project_id, parent_run_id for sub-agent runs, started_at/updated_at, status). Design tokens: app/tokens.ts — CSS variables, both themes must work, zero hardcoded colors.

## Definition of done
1. TIME TRUTH: a settled run (completed/failed/cancelled) shows a FROZEN duration (settled_at - started_at). Only live runs tick. No exceptions anywhere in the panel.
2. KIND TRUTH: every row is visibly classified: full Claude Code session runs (project workers with their role: architect/planner/builder/reviewer/scout/researcher, and operator chats) vs in-process sub-agents (parent_run_id children), with the model it ran on and, on hover, its parent/lineage. A stranger should be able to read the panel and understand the org chart of a running project.
3. HOVER PERFORMANCE: hovering rows causes no visible lag. Profile first (React DevTools profiler or equivalent measurement in the planning corpus), find the actual cause (re-render storm, expensive tooltip mount, layout thrash, over-polling), fix it, and record before/after numbers.
4. AGENT COMMS IN CHAT: in the operator chat thread, messages the operator sends to agents and results/notifications it receives back render as first-class collapsible blocks in the transcript — direction marker + agent name + one-line preview, expandable to the full payload — visually consistent with how Bash tool blocks render. The data already exists in the run's thread JSON (tool_use / tool_result entries for Agent/SendMessage and task notifications); render it, don't invent a new pipeline. If specific payloads truly are not in the thread, document exactly what is missing instead of building new plumbing.
5. npx tsc --noEmit clean in both repos; npm run build passes in forge-control-web.

## Quality bar
Reviewers must run tsc + the web build, curl the touched endpoints, and verify both themes. For the hover fix, the reviewer must see the recorded before/after measurement, not take the builder's word.

## Constraints / hard rules
- Design tokens only. pnpm repos: NODE_ENV=development pnpm add X --prod=false.
- NEVER restart or touch forge-executor. Restarting forge-control and forge-control-web is allowed.
- Do NOT touch Files components (FileExplorerPanel*, VaultFileList*, routes/files.ts) — recently shipped by another project.
- Do NOT touch forge-control/src/lib/project-tick.ts, cc-runner.ts, executor.ts or db/projects.ts — a parallel project (engine-v2-research-lane) owns engine internals this cycle. If a small runs-query change in routes/agents.ts needs a db helper, put it in routes/agents.ts's own query, not in shared engine files.
- Work ONLY inside this worktree until the deploy phase. Never edit the live checkout /opt/forge-ai-os during build phases.

## Deployment (final phase, only after reviewer PASS)
1. In /opt/forge-ai-os: merge main INTO your work branch first if main moved, re-run tsc + build in the worktree, then merge your branch to main. On any conflict: STOP, leave the branch, report exactly which files.
2. Rebuild forge-control-web, pm2 restart forge-control-web (and forge-control only if API files changed). NEVER forge-executor.
3. Verify pm2 online, :7700/api/health ok, web serves. Summarize changes + the hover before/after numbers in your final message.

projects.brief:
## Goal
Harden the goal/project engine using the bugs its first night exposed, then extend it with the deep-research lane Konrad asked for: a researcher role that can steer a real browser, reach external AI services (Perplexity; Gemini specifically for VIDEO quality assurance), plus pragmatic GitHub integration. This is 're-engineering the engineering system' — the engine you are running on is the subject of this project.

## Context
Engine code (forge-control): src/lib/project-tick.ts (orchestrator tick: prompts, promotion, reconciliation, heartbeats), src/db/projects.ts, src/lib/workspace.ts, src/routes/projects.ts, src/lib/cc-runner.ts (run spawning, role files from /root/.claude/agents/<role>.md, cached until executor restart). Read docs/plan corpora of past projects and the vault note 'AI OS/Goal Mode Design.md' for design intent. DB already accepts role 'researcher' and tier 'junior' (migration 0034). Browser automation available via the playwright-skill and hermes browser skills; check /opt/ai-os/.secrets/ for existing API keys before assuming any are missing.

## Known bugs from the first night (Phase: engine hardening — fix ALL of these)
1. DUPLICATE REVIEWER CHAINS: two reviewer tasks in the same round each spawned their own 'Fix cycle 1' builder + re-reviewer, and later duplicate deploy builders — reconcileReviewer() has no dedupe. Design a consolidation: multiple NEEDS_FIXES verdicts in one round must produce exactly ONE fix builder + ONE re-review (merge the feedback), and a PASS from one reviewer must not race another's NEEDS_FIXES.
2. BLOCKED PROJECTS KEEP RUNNING: promoteReadyTasks() and claimReadyTasks() ignore project status — a blocked/paused project's remaining rounds keep spawning runs. Gate both on projects.status = 'active'.
3. LIVE-CHECKOUT HOT-APPLY: fleet agents edited /opt/forge-ai-os (live) during build phases so reviewers could curl real endpoints — that caused unexplained forge-control restarts. Policy decision (design it properly): build phases are worktree-only; verification against live endpoints happens via an explicit, clearly-briefed deploy/verify task, never ad hoc. Encode the rule in the role prompts in project-tick.ts buildPrompt() and make reviewers check `git -C /opt/forge-ai-os status` cleanliness as part of their checklist.
4. EXECUTOR SELF-DEPLOY: when a project's diff touches executor-loaded code (src/lib/project-tick.ts, cc-runner.ts, executor.ts, src/db/*), pm2 restart would kill live runs. The deploy prompt/pattern must instead launch /opt/ai-os/scripts/safe-restart.sh forge-executor DETACHED (setsid nohup ... &) and end; the restart lands when the fleet is idle. Encode this in the goal-mode deploy guidance.

## Research lane (subsequent phases)
5. RESEARCHER ROLE: create /root/.claude/agents/researcher.md — mission: deep research with real sources; may steer a browser (playwright skill) for logged-in/web-app work; must cite what it saw; writes docs/research/*.md. Frontmatter tools should include Read, Write, Glob, Grep, Bash, WebSearch, WebFetch, Skill. project-tick already has a researcher prompt branch.
6. GEMINI VIDEO QA: build a standalone CLI `bin/gemini-qa` (or scripts/) that takes a local video path or URL, sends it to the Gemini API, and returns structured QA JSON (hook/watch-points: pacing, audio glitches, visual artifacts, factual red flags, hook quality — design the rubric). Konrad wants this as the QA backbone for the video pipeline later. If no GEMINI/GOOGLE API key exists in /opt/ai-os/.secrets/, build it cleanly behind GEMINI_API_KEY, prove it against the API's error path, and queue a reminder via POST :7700/api/reminders telling Konrad exactly which key to add and where.
7. PERPLEXITY ACCESS: research the current Perplexity API; implement a thin search/ask helper behind PERPLEXITY_API_KEY with the same missing-key protocol. Browser-steering fallback is acceptable to document but do not build fragile scraping.
8. GITHUB: when a project's base repo has an origin remote and gh is authenticated: push the work branch at each phase completion (never force), and on project completion optionally open a PR instead of merging when the brief says so. Implement in the deploy guidance + a small helper; keep it boring.

## Definition of done
- All four engine bugs fixed with the behavior above, covered by unit tests where the logic is pure (reviewer-verdict consolidation, promotion gating — extract testable functions; there is a test precedent in src/lib/account-health.test.ts).
- researcher.md exists and a smoke researcher task can run end-to-end in a scratch project.
- gemini-qa and perplexity helpers exist, behave correctly with and without keys, with docs.
- GitHub push/PR behavior implemented and documented.
- npx tsc --noEmit clean in forge-control; existing tests plus new ones pass.

## Quality bar
Reviewers run tsc + the test suite, and for engine changes reason through the failure modes explicitly (double-fire, races between ticks, blocked-status transitions mid-round). One phase must include a red-team reviewer briefed to attack the reconciliation logic with concrete scenarios.

## Constraints / hard rules
- You are modifying the engine that runs you. Work ONLY in this worktree during build phases. NEVER edit /opt/forge-ai-os live during build phases. NEVER pm2 restart forge-executor — not even via a builder 'just to test'.
- Do NOT touch forge-control-web/app/desktop/** — a parallel project (operator-visibility) owns the web UI this cycle. API route changes are fine except routes/agents.ts (theirs).
- pnpm rules as always. Design tokens irrelevant here (no UI work).

## Deployment (final phase, only after reviewer PASS)
1. In /opt/forge-ai-os: merge main into your branch first if main moved, re-run tsc + tests in the worktree, then merge to main. Conflicts: STOP and report files.
2. pm2 restart forge-control (API side) is allowed. For the executor-side code: launch /opt/ai-os/scripts/safe-restart.sh forge-executor 43200 45 DETACHED (setsid nohup) and finish — do NOT wait for it.
3. Final message: what changed, test results, which keys/reminders Konrad owes the system.

## Goal
Make the Files experience in forge-control-web genuinely fast and fully correct in light mode. Konrad's words: 'when I click the file section, things still lag and they still don't work in light mode.' This is the overnight proving run for goal mode — quality over speed, but it must be DONE and DEPLOYED by morning.

## Context
Repos inside this worktree: forge-control (Hono API on :7700, tsx runtime) and forge-control-web (Next 15 + React 19, served by pm2 process forge-control-web). The Files UI lives under forge-control-web/app/desktop/ — grep for FileExplorerPanel and the files API routes in forge-control/src/routes/files.ts. Design tokens are CSS variables defined in forge-control-web/app/tokens.ts — the light theme swaps variable values, so any hardcoded hex/rgb in Files components is a bug by definition. Suspects for the lag: fetching too much per click (full directory trees, stat calls), no caching, no virtualization for large directories, blocking renders. Profile before fixing: measure the actual click-to-render path (API timing via curl, component re-renders) and write the findings into the planning corpus.

## Definition of done
- Clicking into the Files section renders visibly within ~200ms on typical directories; large directories (1000+ entries) stay responsive (virtualized or paginated — no frozen main thread).
- No API call in the click path fetches recursively more than the directory being viewed.
- Zero hardcoded colors in Files components — every color reads a token variable; the pane is verified readable and consistent in BOTH light and dark themes.
- npx tsc --noEmit clean in forge-control AND forge-control-web; npm run build passes in forge-control-web.

## Quality bar
The phase reviewer must actually run: tsc in both repos, the web build, curl timings against the files API endpoints, and a grep for hardcoded hex/rgb/hsl literals in the touched components. A review without executed checks is a NEEDS_FIXES on itself.

## Constraints / hard rules
- Design tokens only; never hardcode colors.
- pnpm repos: NODE_ENV=development pnpm add X --prod=false. Never plain npm install.
- NEVER restart or touch forge-executor. Restarting forge-control and forge-control-web is allowed.
- Do not redesign the desktop shell: DesktopApp.tsx and app/desktop/live/ stay untouched unless a one-line integration is strictly unavoidable.
- Keep the diff focused on the Files experience — no drive-by refactors.

## Deployment (final phase, only after the reviewer's PASS)
1. In /opt/forge-ai-os (the live checkout, NOT this worktree): git merge the project work branch into main. If the merge conflicts, STOP — leave the branch, do not force anything, and report the conflict in your final message.
2. Rebuild forge-control-web (pnpm install only if deps changed, then the build) and pm2 restart forge-control-web; restart forge-control only if its files changed. NEVER forge-executor.
3. Verify: pm2 shows both processes online, GET http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/health responds, and the web app serves HTTP 200 on its port (find it via pm2 env/ecosystem config).
4. Leave a summary of what changed and the before/after timings as the final task message.

## Goal
Restructure the desktop UI's two sidebars around Konrad's mental model: LEFT = what he steers, RIGHT = what the selected group is doing. Right now manager-level entries (project/goal runs) show up in the right Live panel mixed across projects — he finds that confusing and wants it fixed.

## The model (Konrad's words, 2026-08-05)
- LEFT rail: his conversations as today, PLUS a managers section — exactly one entry per active project/goal ('one manager basically per project or goal'). Each manager entry shows the group's aggregate token usage/spend and coarse progress (done/total tasks, status). Raw project-task runs must still NEVER appear as individual chats in the rail (the existing project_tasks.run_id exclusion in forge-control/src/db/runs.ts listRuns/searchRuns stays).
- RIGHT Live panel: ONLY the workers of the selected manager's group — that project's architect/planner/builder/reviewer runs and their sub-agents (parent_run_id children), each with per-worker token usage. Never show other projects' manager-level entries there. When no manager is selected, default to the most recently active project's group; provide an obvious way to switch.

## Where things live
- Web: /opt/forge-ai-os/forge-control-web (Next 15 + React 19, pm2 forge-control-web). Live panel components: app/desktop/live/AgentActivity.tsx + agentsApi.ts. Left rail: grep the chat rail components under app/desktop/. Design tokens: app/tokens.ts (CSS variables — both themes must keep working; zero hardcoded colors).
- API: /opt/forge-ai-os/forge-control (Hono :7700, tsx). Projects + tasks: src/routes/projects.ts, src/db/projects.ts (see /board and listActiveTasks). Runs: src/db/runs.ts, src/routes/chat.ts, src/routes/live.ts. Token/spend accounting: src/routes/spend.ts, src/routes/usage.ts and wherever runs store usage — read them to find the real source of truth; if no per-run token rollup exists, add an efficient aggregate endpoint (e.g. GET /api/projects with per-project token/cost rollup, and per-run usage in the group feed). No N+1 queries; aggregate in SQL.

## Definition of done
- Left rail shows a managers section: one card per active/blocked project (name, status, done/total tasks, aggregate tokens or EUR spend). Clicking selects that group. Done/cancelled projects drop off (or collapse under a history toggle).
- Right Live panel shows only the selected group's worker runs + their sub-agents, with per-worker token usage; nothing manager-level from other groups. Non-project standalone runs (e.g. Konrad's own chats) never pollute the Live panel.
- Existing chat behavior in the rail is unchanged for conversations.
- npx tsc --noEmit clean in both repos; npm run build passes in forge-control-web.

## Quality bar
Reviewer must run tsc in both repos, the web build, and curl the new/changed API endpoints against :7700 verifying real JSON (including the token rollup numbers being non-zero for a project that has runs). Grep the touched components for hardcoded hex/rgb/hsl — tokens only. Verify both themes.

## Constraints / hard rules

If your change seems to require it, stop and say so in your final message instead.
- You MAY edit the desktop shell (DesktopApp.tsx, app/desktop/live/) — it is the scope of this project — but keep diffs surgical.
- Design tokens only. pnpm repos: NODE_ENV=development pnpm add X --prod=false. NEVER restart or touch forge-executor; restarting forge-control and forge-control-web is allowed.

## Deployment (final phase, only after the reviewer's PASS)

In /opt/forge-ai-os (live checkout): if main has moved since you branched (the Files project may have merged), first merge main INTO your work branch, re-run tsc + build there, then merge your branch to main. If conflicts arise at any point, STOP, leave the branch, and report exactly which files conflict.

EXISTING: src/lib/excalidraw-md.ts (lossless .excalidraw.md codec, both parsed + LZString compressed-json), src/routes/canvas.ts (GET /list, GET /file?path=, PUT /file mtime-guarded 409, POST /new), app/desktop/CanvasPane.tsx (Excalidraw editor, split-screen beside chat), app/canvas/page.tsx (standalone tab).

IMPLEMENT, in this order:

1) SERVER-SIDE PER-CHAT CANVAS STATE (replaces the localStorage hack in ChatSurface.tsx keyed forge.canvasByRun). Persist which drawing is open for a run in runs.metadata (e.g. metadata.canvas_path + canvas_open), mirroring the existing setRunModel/setRunEffort helpers in src/db/runs.ts and the POST /api/chat/:id/model route in src/routes/chat.ts. Add POST /api/chat/:id/canvas {path, open}. ChatSurface must read it from the run detail and restore the split on open. This makes the canvas survive reloads AND other devices.

2) THE AGENT CAN OPEN A DRAWING IN THE UI. Because state now lives in runs.metadata, the operator agent can just POST /api/chat/:id/canvas to make a drawing appear in Konrad's browser. Make the UI poll/refetch run detail so it opens within a few seconds. Document the exact curl in your summary — Konrad wants to say "open the directory engine map" and have it appear.

4) DRAG AND DROP INTO THE CANVAS. The file explorer already emits a drag payload — grep VPS_FILE_DRAG_MIME in app/desktop/chat/FileExplorerPanel.tsx. (a) Dropping a *.excalidraw.md onto the canvas pane OPENS that drawing. (b) Dropping an image file inserts it into the drawing as an Excalidraw image element. If (b) is too costly, ship (a) and say so.

5) THIN CHAT ROWS WHEN THE CANVAS IS OPEN. In ChatSurface.tsx the chat-list column squeezes the composer when the canvas is open. When canvasOpen, render each chat row compact: status dot + relative time + first ~2 words only.

HARD RULES: DO NOT EDIT app/desktop/DesktopApp.tsx, app/tokens.ts, or anything under app/desktop/live/ — other engineers hold those. Use tokens from app/tokens.ts (CSS vars — never hardcode hex, light mode must keep working). Repos are pnpm: NODE_ENV=development pnpm add X --prod=false. Verify: npx tsc --noEmit in both repos, npm run build in the web repo, and curl every new endpoint against :7700 to prove real responses.

projects.brief:
Run a script-writing campaign for the faceless YouTube channel "The Sky Lab" (space-weather / cosmic-threat documentaries). These scripts are fed to the ReelForge video engine, which renders each into a 60-90 min faceless documentary. This is a coding-style project only in mechanism; the deliverables are narration scripts, not code.

STEP 1 (you, the architect): Read these vault files for the exact voice, structure, and HARD rules — you have vault access, the builders do NOT, so you must distill everything they need into each builder brief:
- /opt/obsidian-vault/30_YouTube/TheSkyLab/faceless_scripting_sop.md
- /opt/obsidian-vault/30_YouTube/TheSkyLab/faceless_channel_strategy.md
- /opt/obsidian-vault/30_YouTube/TheSkyLab/TheSkyLab Production Slate.md

STEP 2: Fan out exactly SIX builder tasks (tier "standard"), one per remaining slate topic below. Do NOT write scripts yourself.
- 07 "Solar Cycle 25: Why the Sun Overperformed" — SIDC/SWPC sunspot numbers, the 2019 NOAA/NASA prediction panel forecast vs the actual overperformance, AR3664, solar maximum.
- 08 "Coronal Holes and the High-Speed Solar Wind" — DSCOVR/ACE at L1, recurrent coronal-hole streams, 27-day solar rotation recurrence, high-speed streams and G1-G2 storms.
- 10 "Geomagnetic Reversals and the Laschamp Excursion" — ~41,000-yr-ago Laschamp excursion, paleomagnetism, cosmogenic Be-10, present dipole decay ~5%/century, the South Atlantic Anomaly link.
- 11 "Interstellar Visitors: 'Oumuamua and Borisov" — 1I/2017 U1 'Oumuamua (Pan-STARRS, Oct 2017, non-gravitational acceleration debate), 2I/Borisov (Aug 2019, first clearly cometary interstellar object).
- 12 "Betelgeuse and the Great Dimming" — the 2019-2020 dimming, VLT/SPHERE imaging, dust-clump vs convection-cell explanation, supernova distance (~168 pc) and what a nearby SN would and would not do to Earth.
- 13 "The Day the Satellites Fell: February 2022 Starlink Loss" — the ~38-40 Starlink satellites lost after a minor G1 storm raised thermospheric density and atmospheric drag right after a Feb 3 2022 launch.

STEP 3 EACH BUILDER BRIEF MUST EMBED (verbatim rules, because builders can't read the vault):
- Deliverable: write ONE script file to scripts/NN-slug.md inside the worktree (create the scripts/ dir), then commit it. NN = the topic number above.
- PURE SPOKEN NARRATION only — this text goes straight to text-to-speech. NO markdown headers, no "#", no chapter titles, no [MUSIC]/[PAUSE]/visual cues, no bullet lists, no stage directions. Paragraphs separated by a single blank line. TTS reads every character literally.
- Length target ~10,000-12,000 words. IMPORTANT: prioritise FINISHING with a clean closing outro over maximum length — a complete 10k-word script beats a truncated 14k one. End with a low-key analytical takeaway and a soft CTA to subscribe to The Sky Lab.
- Voice: serious investigative science-documentary; measured, calm, slightly ominous, data-anchored. Vary sentence length hard (a three-word sentence beside a forty-word one). Hyper-specific numbers and dates throughout.
- HARD RULE — REAL DATA ONLY: every number, date, named event, instrument (SDO, SOHO, DSCOVR, ACE, GOES, Swarm, Pan-STARRS, VLT), and institution (NOAA SWPC, NASA, ESA, JAXA) must be real and verifiable. Use WebSearch to verify. NEVER fabricate telemetry, invent designations, or invent "breaking" events.
- Banned words: "delve","leverage","comprehensive","robust","holistic","in conclusion","thus","incredible","unbelievable","mind-blowing","cosmic secrets","alien mystery". Omit or use plain equivalents.
- Builder must self-check before reporting done: file is pure prose (grep -c for '#','[MUSIC]','CHAPTER' = 0), ends cleanly, word count >= 9000.

STEP 4: End with exactly ONE reviewer task (round after the last builder round) briefed to check every scripts/*.md for: markdown/cue contamination (must be zero), a clean SkyLab outro, length >= 9000 words, banned-word hits, and obviously fabricated/unverifiable data. VERDICT: PASS only if all six are clean.
